//verification: The one thing this repository cannot work out for you: what checks this project has, and where the change stops being under your control once it ships. artifact_kind: service | library | cli | chart | migration | model-boundary | plugin.

stage2: v=$(cat VERSION); d=$(mktemp -d); helm pull oci://ghcr.io/concordloom/charts/loomwatch --version "$v" -d "$d" && helm template lw "$d/loomwatch-$v.tgz" > /dev/null && rm -rf "$d"
verification.notes:
Stage 2 runs against the deployed instance. Its address and credentials are machine-local and live in gopnik.local.env, which .gitignore keeps out of commits.

The first command reaches the service through a port-forward rather than a public address. The panel used to be published through an ingress with a DNS record and a certificate, which meant a human interface with one password and no second factor answered the internet so that a few administrative actions a year would be convenient. Those actions are declarative now - subscriptions are named in the chart's auth.accounts - so the interface stayed and the exposure went. scripts/check-deployed.sh opens the forward, proves the deployed revision from the login page and from onwatch_build_info, runs the browser check with its own negative case, and tears the forward down.

Delivery is post-release and manual: pushing a loom-v* tag publishes the image and the chart, and the deployment is moved to that version by hand afterwards, so a Stage 2 run gates the release rather than the merge, and it fails until the deployment has actually been moved to the revision under test. The last cell covers the chart surface by pulling the published artifact for this revision and rendering it.

tests/js/dashboard-test.js is deliberately not in stage1 - nothing in the repository installs its npm dependencies, so it cannot run here. integration_test.go sits behind //go:build integration, which none of the stage1 commands passes, so `go vet -tags integration ./...` is the only thing that compiles it; a change that edits that file should run it rather than assume Stage 1 covered it.
